explain.say: Have you ever had a burning tummy after a big spicy meal? Some people take an antacid tablet, and it calms the acid down. That is neutralisation! Look at the board. You start with hydrochloric acid, full of H plus ions.

explain.say: Water! Now look at the graph. As you add alkali, the pH starts low, then shoots up through 7, and levels off high. Add exactly the right amount and the solution is neutral, pH 7. Where do you see the steepest part of the curve?

Right in the middle! Great work, you read it like a scientist. The sodium and the chloride stay in the water as sodium chloride: table salt. So acid plus alkali gives salt plus water. Wow: farmers in India and Kenya spread lime on acidic soil to neutralise it, so crops grow better.

faq.a: Hydrogen ions from the acid react with hydroxide ions from the alkali to make water. The other ions stay behind as a salt.
asks: What is the ionic equation for neutralisation?

faq.q: What salt does each acid make?
faq.a: Hydrochloric acid makes chlorides, sulfuric acid makes sulfates, and nitric acid makes nitrates. So sodium hydroxide plus sulfuric acid gives sodium sulfate.
asks: How do you name a salt?

faq.a: Antacid tablets contain bases, like calcium carbonate or magnesium hydroxide, which neutralise some of the extra acid in your stomach.
A titration is a careful way to add exactly enough alkali to neutralise an acid, using a burette and an indicator to spot the end point.
asks: How do you find exactly how much alkali to add?

faq.q: Why is lime added to soil?
faq.a: Lime, calcium hydroxide or calcium carbonate, is a base. It neutralises acidic soil, so crops that need a near-neutral pH can grow well.
asks: How do farmers fix acidic soil?

facts: The ionic equation for neutralisation is H+ + OH- → H2O.
Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide react to form sodium chloride and water: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O.
